about: Facts the certificate must keep. scripts/check_fidelity.py checks each one against facts.json, so that a change to Certificate/Facts.lean cannot quietly lose them. They answer Astra's outside review (docs/reports/outside-review-01.md), which asked for these regressions by name; brief 0005, stage 1k. Each names an entry by its ref and a field of it (Certificate/FIELDS.md), and asks that the list `includes` some names, `excludes` others, or holds exactly `count.is` names beginning with `count.prefix`; `equals` compares the field with a value. A field that is an object, as `inherited` is, is read by its keys, and a field the entry lacks fails. A field that is a list of objects, as `cited_laws` is, is read by each object's `law`; with `law`, an expectation reads that cited law's `construction_rules` instead. An expectation with no `ref` reads a field of the top level of facts.json, as `construction_rules` is. One with `"every": "entry"` and no `ref` reads its field in every entry, porisms and companions included, and asks only that it `excludes` some names; there a list of objects, as `shared_steps` is, is read by each object's `name`. `why` is shown when one fails.

expectations.why: The porism's own entry pins every assumption of its proof by the argument of Euclid's reductio from the given centre: since the second retirement, 38 tacit rules, counted separately from III.1's construction. Since Book Zero came to rest on the radius rule (#473), radius_ne_zero stands among them where circle_eq stood, and the count is unchanged. Since centre_unique is now a theorem, excluding its name from axioms cannot detect a call to it; the pin on the porism's proved_rules, below, can (#168). The proof neither calls III.1 nor uses exists_centre.

III.1's certificate now also carries exists_centre, for D within by III.2's argument inside its construction and for the supposed centre G of its reductio, and the entry pins it by name, so that the count alone cannot hide it giving way to another rule: since the second retirement, 39 tacit rules, counted separately from its porism. Since centre_unique is now a theorem, excluding its name from axioms cannot detect a call to it; the claim that this proof avoids it rests on proof review.
A porism's entry names its proposition.
A proposition lists its porism, so that it is not complete until the porism is proved.

III.2's own Lean does not call Circle 2 (Argon's second review; #65). Circle 2 has been a theorem since 19 October 2026, so excluding its name from own_axioms cannot detect a call to it; nor can the axioms pin's exclusion of Circle 3, a theorem too since 24 October 2026 (#294). Both are now proved after III.2, in Elements/BookIII/Prop02.lean, from its corollary Prop2.within, and a proof of III.2 cannot use a theorem proved from III.2, since Lean admits no circular proof.

No lemma that III.2 calls uses Circle 2 (#65). Circle 2 has been a theorem since 19 October 2026, so excluding its name from inherited cannot detect such a use; nor can the axioms pin's exclusion of Circle 3, a theorem too since 24 October 2026 (#294). Both are now proved after III.2, from its corollary Prop2.within, so no lemma that III.2 calls can use either: Lean admits no circular proof.

This pin once checked that III.2 did not rest on Circle 3, then an axiom, and kept Circle 2's retired name out of its axiom list (#60). What keeps III.2 off them now is Lean: a proof of III.2 cannot use a theorem proved from III.2, since Lean admits no circular proof.

Circle 2 has been a theorem since 19 October 2026 and Circle 3 since 24 October; both are now proved after III.2 (#294), so excluding their names from axioms can no longer fail. A proof that used either would cite III.2, since the walk that finds an entry's cites passes through proved rules (the II.1 pin), and check_fidelity refuses III.1's citing III.2, which does not come before it; the pin on III.1's cites, next, can fail.

#60's claim that III.1 does not rest on Circle 3 now takes this form (#294): III.1 does not cite III.2, as a proof using Circle 2, Circle 3, Points 9 or Intersection 2 would. All four are proved after III.2 since 24 October 2026, and a proof that uses any of them cites III.2, for the walk that finds an entry's cites passes through proved rules, as the II.1 pin shows.

A construction rule is an axiom whose conclusion asserts existence once the project's definitions are unfolded (docs/FORMALIZATION.md, section 9): the postulates that draw, the rules that give a point, and those that conclude CirclesMeet or LinesMeet are among them. A rule that concludes an equality, a negation, OutsideCircle, an order read through its instance, or the restricted rule is not. Every rule it requires is still an axiom, and so is every rule it excludes but two: Tacit.pasch3, which the second retirement wave proves as a theorem, and Tacit.outside_of_between (Circle 3), which concludes OutsideCircle and has been a theorem since 24 October 2026, proved after III.2 (#294). A theorem is in no list of axioms, so excluding those two can no longer fail (#150, question 4).
